introduction.sri_rudram: Sri Rudram, a hymn to Sri Rudra - the fierce aspect of Lord Shiv - is found in the Taittiriya Samhita of the Krishna Yajurved. It consists of two hymns: Namakam and Chamakam. Sri Rudram is a powerful prayer to invoke Lord Rudra's grace for self-purification and Prayashchit (atonement).
introduction.origin_story: Guided by Sri Vishnu, Devas were the first ones to offer Sri Rudram Stuti to Mahadev after the completion of Samudra Manthan (Churning of the Cosmic Ocean). Later, Lord Kartikeya wanted to know if it was correct on the Devas' part to have all the nectar (Amrit) to themselves. His doubts were resolved by Ma Parvati, who gave him knowledge of Sri Rudram. From Lord Kartikeya, the stotram got passed on to sage Jaigishavya.
introduction.program_note: Under Om Swami ji's guidance, the rare Maharudra Sadhana was performed - going back to the Vedic era and learning about the sages who invoked various Sri Rudram mantras (Namakam).

rishis.purpose: Maharishi Kashyap wanted to do Prayashchit for begetting the Asuras Hiranyaksh and Hiranyakashipu, as he had coupled with his wife Diti at an inappropriate moment. Kashyap Muni received Sri Rudram from his Guru, Maharishi Jaigishavya.

Maharishi Atri, the Manas Putra (mind-born son) of Lord Brahma, had three sons: Dattatreya, Durvasa, and Som. With the help of Sri Rudram, Atri rishi secured the freedom of Suryadev, who had been abducted by Swarbhanu (Rahu).

Maharishi Pulastya invoked the most verses of Sri Rudram (55 in total). Rishi Pulastya received the knowledge of Sri Rudram from Devrishi Narad. Later, impressed by the penance and determination of the Asura king Ravan (his grandson), Maharishi Pulastya gave him the knowledge of Sri Rudram.
Maharishi Gautam invoked two verses of Sri Rudram to do Prayashchit for cursing his wife Ahalya in anger and turning her into a stone. He received Sri Rudram sadhana from Sri Vishnu Himself.

Devrishi Narad wanted to do Prayaschit for having cursed his deity, Lord Narayan, who had given Narad a monkey face (hari mukh) as part of His Divine leela to break Narad's ego. Devrishi Narad knew Sri Rudram from the time it was first recited by the Devas; however, he got specific instructions (Sri Rudram Sadhana Vidhi) from Maharishi Pulastya.
Maharishi Durvasa wanted to perform Prayaschit, as he had turned his wife, Kadali, into ashes. Sage Durvasa received the knowledge of Sri Rudram directly from Mahadev.

Maharishi Pulaha received the Sri Rudram knowledge from Lord Kartikeya and used it for the welfare of the marginalised community of Kinpurush. He also imparted Anuvak 7 to King Bheemak and a Brahmin called Hemkosh.

Deval Rishi got the knowledge of Sri Rudram from Devi Jagadamba, Ma Parvati. He wanted to do Prayashchit for having doubted an accomplished sage, Maharishi Jaigishavya. Deval Rishi also used the knowledge of the Sri Rudram for world welfare.

Mandavya Rishi, falsely accused of theft, was punished with a spear pierced through his body. Later, his innocence was proven, and he was freed. Unable to understand the karmic basis of his intense suffering, Mandavya Rishi invoked Dharmaraj. Dharmaraj explained that the suffering had resulted from a violent act of torturing a dragonfly - a crime committed by the sage as a five-year-old, 101 lifetimes ago. Angered by the injustice, Rishi Mandavya cursed Dharmaraj to be born as a human, and later regretted it. To perform Prayashchit, Sage Mandavya received the knowledge of Sri Rudram directly from Lord Shiv.

Kanav Rishi had Garbh Siddhi to protect pregnant women and their unborn child. During a yagna in Dwarka, Sri Krishna's son, Samba, and other Yadav boys played an audacious prank. Dressed as a pregnant woman (a pestle tied to his stomach), Samba and his friends asked Rishi Kanav about the gender and well-being of the unborn child. Sensing their arrogance, sage Kanav predicted that what Samba carried would lead to the complete destruction of the Yadav clan. When Sri Krishna died, Kanav Rishi repented his curse. Guided by Maharishi Ved Vyas, he performed prayashchit with Sri Rudram, invoking verses 6 and 7 of Anuvak 1.

After the Samudra Manthan, Devas had prayed in order to pacify Lord Shiv's fierce aspect, repeatedly requesting him to put his bow (Pinak) down. Mahadev kept the bow down and decided (along with Devas) to entrust its safekeeping to Shiv Upasak and the King of Mithila, Devrath Janak. In order to offer Nitya puja to Pinak, Sri Vishnu gave the knowledge of Sri Rudram to Devrath Janak, who also invoked two verses in Anuvak 10 of Namakam. Lord Parshuram, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu, was the protector of the bow.
